title: Idempotents lift uniquely along a base change of a nilpotent thickening
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$, $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $Y_0=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and $i:Y_0\to Y$ the first projection. Then (1) $i$ is a closed immersion whose quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $\mathcal J$ satisfies $\mathcal J^N=0$, so $Y$ is a finite order thickening of $Y_0$ and $i$ is a homeomorphism of underlying topological spaces [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]; (2) the ring map $i^\sharp:\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ induces a bijection from the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ to the set of idempotents of $\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$: every idempotent of $\Gamma(Y_0,\mathcal O_{Y_0})$ is $i^\sharp(e)$ for exactly one idempotent $e\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 09ZU (lemma-base-change-thickening, line 209; proof omitted) with Definition Tag 04EX (definition-thickening, line 36) for (1); (2) is the step of Derived Categories, proof of Lemma Tag 0G7X (perfect.tex lines 8137-8146: 'Since the underlying topological space of X_n is equal to that of X_s we obtain ... a nontrivial idempotent e_n'), via idempotents <-> open and closed subsets (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00EE)

mathlib_searches.query: idempotents of a ring lift uniquely modulo a nilpotent ideal; closed immersion defined by nilpotent ideal is a homeomorphism of schemes
mathlib_searches.results: existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent, exists_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent, OrthogonalIdempotents.lift_of_isNilpotent_ker (Mathlib.RingTheory.Idempotents): ring-level only; for a non-affine Y the kernel of Gamma(Y,O_Y) -> Gamma(Y_0,O_{Y_0}) need not be nil, so these do not give (2) in one line

mathlib_searches.query: thickening of schemes: a closed immersion with nilpotent ideal sheaf is a homeomorphism, so idempotent global sections correspond

mathlib_searches.results: only FormallyUnramified.lean:189 (docstring 'infinitesimal thickening') and OpenImmersion.lean:38 (ker spanned by an idempotent); no thickening/idempotent lemma for schemes
